sources.citation: 吴正彪、杨光应. 2010. 麻山次方言区苗文方案的设计与使用—兼谈苗族英雄史诗《亚鲁王》的记译整理问题. 民族翻译 2010(3): 58-65.
sources.note: Central Mashan (Zongdi, Dadiba) orthography with initials, finals and 11 tone values; a full-text search for stress/accent 重音/轻声/轻读/轻音 finds nothing. Central, not Northern.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2007. Change Request 2007-129 (adds name 'Miao, Northern Mashan').
sources.note: Naming request only; cites Enwall 1994-95, Hattaway 2000, Wang & Mao 1995. Nothing linguistic.

sources.citation: Purnell, Herbert C. (ed.). 1972. Miao and Yao Linguistic Studies (Cornell SEAP Data Paper 88), incl. Miao Language Team 1962 'A brief description of the Miao language'
sources.note: Mashan subdialect represented by Chiao yi, Ziyun (Central); Mashan lacks uvular stops; 'stress' does not occur in the Miao chapters.
sources.venue: Miao Language Team 1962 'A brief description of the Miao language'

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en) 'Mashan Miao language' (raw wikitext) and Omniglot 'Mashan Miao', accessed 2026-09-17
sources.note: No stress statement. Northern Mang 35,000 (Li 2018: 30,000; Changshun, Huishui, Luodian; Wang 1985 datapoint given as 摆梭乡, Changshun, whereas Wang 1985:105 itself names 代化); tone tables only for Central villages (11-13 tones); references Wang 1985, Li Yunbing 2000/2018, Xian 1990, Wu & Yang 2010, Sun & Ting 2017, Heal 2020.

sources.citation: Heal, Sarah. 2020. Grammar Sketch of Mashan Miao. SIL e-Books 74. Dallas: SIL International. viii+75 pp. (speakers LY = Central Mashan [hmm], WZ = Southern Mashan [hma]; Northern vernacular only named)
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Nothing. RRG syntax sketch; a full-text search for stress/accent/'accent' finds none (only 'intonation pause' in the RRG definitions). p.6: four vernaculars Central, Northern, Western, Southern, differences 'mostly to do with tones and vowels (Mortensen 2013:12)'; p.7: 'The tonal system of Mashan Miao is one of the most complex (Mortensen 2013)'; Appendix C pp.71-72 gives Southern-vernacular consonant/vowel/tone tables only (9 tones). No Northern Mashan data.

sources.citation: Schiering, René & Harry van der Hulst. 2010. Word accent systems in the languages of Asia. In van der Hulst, Goedemans & van Zanten (eds.), A Survey of Word Accentual Patterns in the Languages of the World, ch.10.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, paywalled at the publisher
sources.note: Lists 'Northern Mashan Hmong' under CHUANQIANDIAN with only the family-level remark: 'Hmong-Mien is usually described as being exclusively tonal.. Unfortunately, we did not have access to sources that would allow us to elaborate on this point.' No data.
sources.venue: A Survey of Word Accentual Patterns in the Languages of the World, ch.10

tone.quote: Classification Hmong-Mien, Hmongic, Chuanqiandian A member of macrolanguage Hmong [ hmn ] ( China ). Comments Part of Miao nationality. Tonal, 13 tones. Traditional religion.
tone.locator: Ethnologue 16 web entry 'Miao, Northern Mashan' (hmp), fields 'Classification' and 'Comments'
tone.says: Ethnologue 16 'Comments' field states only: 'Tonal, 13 tones.' No tone categories, pitch values, sandhi or source for the count are given (secondhand catalogue statement; the origin of the figure 13 is not stated in the entry and was not verified).
tone.source_kind: database or survey citing another work

sources.citation: Mortensen, David. 2006. Diachronic universals and synchronic parochialisms: explaining tone-vowel interactions (Shuijingping ms., pitt.edu); Mortensen 2013 JEAL 22(3):189-216 and 2006 UC Berkeley dissertation sec. 3.2.3 (held by the project)
sources.note: Central Mashan (Shuijingping) tone system, sandhi and tonally conditioned vowel raising; the 'accent 1/accent 2' passage concerns Limburgian; 'metrical facts' are dismissed as a conditioning factor (2013:190). No mention of Northern Mashan or of Mashan word stress.

sources.citation: 王辅世 (Wang Fushi) 主编. 1985. 苗语简志. 北京: 民族出版社. 2+203 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. p.105: '(2) 北部土语 使用人数约有二万五千。通行在贵州省长顺县代化，罗甸县边阳，惠水县董上等地。' (demography only). p.6: Mashan yin tones split by old aspiration; '固有词每个音节都是由声母、韵母和声调组成'. p.107: Chuanqiandian tone sandhi '相当复杂.. 麻山次方言变调时，韵母也随之改变'. The phonology chapter treats Dananshan, not Mashan; the only 轻声 remark (p.12) concerns Layiping (Xiangxi) prefixes; 重音 never occurs.
sources.venue: 北京: 民族出版社. 2+203 pp

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid nort1546 and family node mash1238 (Hammarström et al.); hh.bib entries tagged [hmp]
